_provenance: Public migration/vendor-exit cases for the FDK lock-in deltaR^2 test. Figures are from public reports where cited, else marked low-confidence recollections to VERIFY. This is a SEED catalogue, not a validated dataset; many outcome fields are unknown (null). Compiled 2026-06-19 with web access; see 'source' on each record.
schema: case, org, from_vendor, to_target, year, migration_cost_usd (or null), duration_months (or null), outcome (success|partial|failure|ongoing|unknown), lock_in_incident (string or null), est_lockin_score_hint[0-1] (rough prior for how locked-in they were BEFORE leaving), source, confidence(low|medium|high)

records.note: SEC pre-IPO filings: ~$75M operating-cost reduction over two years (2016-2017). Still uses AWS for <10% of storage and for EU serving. Savings figure is cited; migration_cost itself not separately disclosed.
records.source: GeekWire (2018), SEC S-1 filing; builtin.com Magic Pocket writeup

records.to_target: Owned Dell hardware in colo; Pure Storage for S3 replacement
records.lock_in_incident: AWS S3 egress: ~$250k egress bill waived by AWS on exit (egress cost is itself a lock-in friction).
records.note: DHH writeups. ~$700k Dell hardware recouped within 2023; ~$2M/yr cloud-bill reduction; projected >$10M over 5yr. Remaining ~$1.3M/yr was S3, now being replaced with ~18PB Pure Storage. AWS account deletion completed 2025.
records.source: DHH/37signals blog; DataCenterDynamics (2024); The Register (2024, 2025); The Stack

records.to_target: OpenStack-based private cloud on Open Compute Project hardware
records.lock_in_incident: Costs grew ~2.5x over expectation to >$300M/yr with declining reliability after a decade-long migration of 600+ apps INTO Azure.
records.note: Repatriating at least ~50% of workloads. Outcome still in progress; cost of repatriation not disclosed.

records.lock_in_incident: AWS contract: ~$510M / 5.5yr take-or-pay commitment (pay regardless of usage). Google Cloud payments halted then resumed (~$300M in 2023). Datacenter downsizing was paused after an outage.
records.note: Claimed ~$100M/yr savings from exiting Sacramento; ~60% monthly cloud-cost reduction by moving media/blobs on-prem. Required moving 5,200 racks / ~148,000 servers. Reliability incidents during the push.
records.source: DataCenterDynamics; The Information; Computer Weekly; Reuters

records.note: AVOIDED lock-in case, not an exit. Claims ~$400M saved over 3yr (later framed over 6yr: $122M owned vs ~$1.1B on cheapest AWS). $1.5k/server/mo vs ~$17.5k AWS-equivalent. migration_cost_usd here is their actual 6yr owned-hardware spend, not a migration.
records.source: Ahrefs engineering blog (Efim Mirochnik); The Register (2023); Techerati; InfoQ

records.lock_in_incident: FORCED EXIT: AWS suspended service ~midnight 2021-01-10 for ToS violation; no pre-built portability. Site offline for days/weeks; mobile apps removed by Apple/Google. Court denied injunction to compel AWS to restore service.
records.note: Canonical 'involuntary exit / no exit plan' case. Demonstrates platform/provider control risk independent of price. Cost not public.
records.source: GeekWire; CNBC; BuzzFeed News; DataCenterDynamics; TechCrunch (2021)

records.lock_in_incident: ~1,000% VMware cost increase under Broadcom triggered the move of 20,000+ VMs.
records.note: Concrete named VMware-exit driven by Broadcom repricing. Migration cost not disclosed.

records.lock_in_incident: 800-1,500% price hikes after per-core subscription model; cease-and-desist letters to subscription-less users; lawsuits (e.g. vs Siemens US).
records.note: Cohort/aggregate row, not a single org. CloudBolt: ~86% of N. American enterprises trying to reduce VMware footprint but only ~4% fully migrated; ~63% changed strategy 2+ times. Illustrates HIGH lock-in + LOW completion (exits are hard even when strongly motivated).
records.source: CloudBolt research via Network World / TechRadar / The Register (2023-2026)

records.lock_in_incident: Jan 2023 shift to per-EMPLOYEE pricing; reported 3x-10x cost increases; aggressive 'soft audit' -> formal audit pipeline; ULA/cloud-subscription upsell as audit settlement (deepens lock-in).
records.note: Classic licensing/audit lock-in. Many migrate to OpenJDK; some settle into larger Oracle commitments. Aggregate row.

records.lock_in_incident: Take-or-pay style cloud commitments: ~$2B/5yr to Google Cloud and ~$1B/5yr to AWS disclosed around IPO; large committed spend is itself a soft lock-in even when multi-cloud.
records.note: Not an exit; included as a multi-cloud-hedge / commitment example. Figures are the headline commitment sizes from IPO-era reporting; treat as approximate. VERIFY exact terms.

Counter-example: GitLab publicly considered moving to bare metal (~2016-2017) and decided to STAY on cloud. Useful as a 'did NOT exit, deliberately' data point against survivorship bias. Details from GitLab public infra blog/issue threads. VERIFY specifics.
records.source: GitLab public infrastructure blog / issue tracker - recollection, verify

records.note: Context row: 37signals had moved some workloads INTO cloud before the 2022 reversal; the round-trip is itself evidence about how reversible cloud decisions are. Distinct from the 2022 exit record. Low precision.
AVOIDED-cloud case: long ran on a small on-prem footprint and published detailed hardware posts. Later did adopt more cloud/Azure. Included as a low-lock-in stay. VERIFY current state.
records.source: Stack Overflow / Nick Craver architecture posts - recollection, verify

records.lock_in_incident: Broadcom litigation against Siemens US over VMware usage/support entitlements - lock-in surfacing as a legal dispute rather than a clean exit.
records.note: Included as a 'lock-in incident becomes litigation' data point. Facts contested and evolving; outcome unknown.
records.source: Trade press reporting via Network World / The Register (2025) - verify

records.lock_in_incident: Reported up to ~1,500% price increases in Europe; Broadcom declined to backtrack per EU cloud watchdog. Regulatory rather than technical exit path.
records.note: Shows that when technical exit is too costly, customers pursue REGULATORY exit - relevant to a legitimacy/decision layer. Aggregate.

records.lock_in_incident: Reported driver: cloud costs exceeding forecasts; a frequently-cited (and frequently-disputed) survey stat is that a large majority of CIOs have repatriated at least one workload.
records.note: Deliberately included as a NOISY aggregate to keep the catalogue honest: survey headlines (e.g. '86% of CIOs repatriating') are marketing-adjacent and not measured outcomes. Do not treat as a measured case.
records.source: Various vendor/analyst surveys (CIODive, a16z 'Cost of Cloud') - low trust
